customer.name: Fictia Beach Kiosk Ltd
customer.occupation: Beach food and drink kiosk operator

scenario.customer: Private limited company operating one kiosk on a public beach under a municipal concession. Business current account used for takings, wages and suppliers.
scenario.alert: Cash credited in the last 90 days is several times the monthly average expected from the customer profile.
scenario.priorWork: Customer is a kiosk, so some cash is expected. Cash value is higher than the profile average. Escalated for full review.

documents.document: One kiosk, open from May to September. Expected annual turnover EUR 190,000, with about 70% earned from June to September. Customers pay by cash or card.
Incorporated in 2021. One director, who also holds 100% of the shares. No other appointments are listed.
Cash is paid in by two people, each with a completed deposit slip naming the kiosk. Deposits are made at the branch nearest the beach.

Accounts prepared by an external accountant, with daily till reports for the season. Average sale EUR 9, about 300 sales a day in peak months, and six seasonal staff. Till totals match the card settlements and cash deposits.
The director explains that nearly all income is earned in summer and supplies the previous year's statements, which show the same seasonal peak. The two depositors are named as the kiosk supervisors.

Invoice for two commercial freezer units from Exampleland Cold Chain Equipment Co, with a customs entry showing the delivery to the kiosk's storage unit. The amounts match the two international payments.

reportBlocks.block: The company deposited a lot of cash during the quarter and also made several payments.

Over the 90-day review period, cash credited to the company's account was several times the monthly average in its profile. It was paid in by two individuals. Funds were also sent to a company overseas.
The director's explanation shows that the funds may be criminal proceeds.
The cash is well above the customer's monthly average, and two international payments went to a company in a higher-risk country.
Beach kiosks are a high-risk sector, so the cash in this account is likely to be criminal.
The director was told that a report would be made, so that further documents could be provided.
The case was referred to the Compliance Officer with the supporting documents. The customer has not been told about the referral.

answer.explanation: The alert compares a peak season with an annual average. The customer declared at onboarding that about 70% of turnover is earned from June to September, and the cash and card receipts fit that share. Till reports reconcile to the deposits, prior-year statements show the same peak, payroll and stock purchases fit the volume, and an invoice with a customs entry supports the payments overseas.
